items.title: Section: How Stillness and Insight Are Actually Attained

items.zh: 初名下士，次名中士，後名上士。復依修習思惟方便建立三人。一者、有人唯得勵力運轉思惟；二者、有人有間運轉，設得無間，要作功用方能運轉；三者、有人已得成就任運思惟。初名下士，次名中士，後名上士。又依己得修差別故建立三人。一者、有人已得內心奢摩他定，未得增上慧法毘鉢舍那；二者、有人已得增上慧法毘鉢舍那，未得內心奢摩他定；三者、有人俱得二種。初名下士，次名中士，後名上士。
items.en: The first is a lower person, the second middling, the third superior, completing seven sections on precepts. There are also three kinds of person by the method of contemplation in cultivation. One who attains only effortful, strenuous contemplation; one whose contemplation is intermittent, requiring real effort even when uninterrupted; one who has attained spontaneous, effortless contemplation. The first is a lower person, the second middling, the third superior. There are also three kinds of person by what has already been attained in cultivation. One who has attained inner calm-abiding, without insight into the higher wisdom-teaching; one who has attained insight into the higher wisdom-teaching, without inner calm-abiding; one who has attained both together. The first is a lower person, the second middling, the third superior.

items.title: Section: Ten Gateways Complete, and Ten Beings' Own Ten Delights

items.zh: 又有三人。一者、有人已得有尋有伺三摩地；二者、有人已得無尋唯伺三摩地；三者、有人已得無尋無伺三摩地。初名下士，次名中士，後名上士。又依住修差別建立三人。一者、有人住染污靜慮；二者、有人住世間清淨靜慮；三者、有人住無漏靜慮。初名下士，次名中士，後名上士。復次，有十種有情眾，於十種法愛樂喜悅。何等十法？一、壽，二、色，三、財，四、友，五、戒，六、聞，七、梵行，八、慧，九、法，十、生天。
items.en: There are also three kinds of person. One who has attained absorption with investigation and reflection; one who has attained absorption with reflection alone; one who has attained absorption without investigation or reflection. The first is a lower person, the second middling, the third superior. There are also three kinds of person by the absorption dwelt within. One who dwells in defiled absorption; one who dwells in worldly pure absorption; one who dwells in undefiled absorption. The first is a lower person, the second middling, the third superior. The above establishes the distinction of lower, middling, and superior persons through ten major sections. Furthermore, there are ten kinds of beings who delight and rejoice in ten kinds of things. What are the ten things? First, life; second, beauty; third, wealth; fourth, friends; fifth, precepts; sixth, learning; seventh, pure conduct; eighth, wisdom; ninth, the Dharma; tenth, heavenly rebirth.

items.title: Section: Ten Beings Named, and Six Faults in Hearing the Dharma

items.zh: 何等名為有情十眾？一、傍生，二、母邑，三、受用欲者，四、求所作者，五、出家者，六、多聞為命者，七、入證者，八、尋思者，九、勤苦者，十、棄身者。復次，聽聞正法者，略有六種煩惱過失。謂憍慢過失、不欲過失、不信過失、身心損惱過失、散亂過失、迷惑過失。由如是等諸過失故，不能恭敬殷重聽法，廣說如經。散亂煩惱過失復有二種。謂說時散亂、說已散亂。迷惑者，謂顛倒。
items.en: What are the ten kinds of beings? First, animals; second, women; third, those who enjoy desires; fourth, those seeking to accomplish something; fifth, renunciants; sixth, those who live by learning; seventh, those who have entered realisation; eighth, contemplative persons; ninth, diligent persons; tenth, those who relinquish the body. There are also six afflictive faults, briefly stated, in one who hears the true Dharma: the fault of arrogance, the fault of unwillingness, the fault of disbelief, the fault of distress to body and mind, the fault of distraction, and the fault of confusion. Because of such faults, one cannot hear the Dharma with reverence and earnestness, as extensively explained in the sutras. The fault of distraction has two further kinds: distraction while the teaching is being spoken, and distraction after it has been spoken. Confusion means inversion.

items.title: Section: Three Ways Affliction Sparks Karma, Six Things No One Loves

items.zh: 復次，煩惱發業略有三種。一、相應發，二、親生發，三、增上發。引餘煩惱而發起故。復次，非所愛法略有六種。一、怨敵，二、疾病，三、不可愛境，四、生等諸苦，五、苦辛良藥，六、非串習善。前四應遠離，後二應修習。
items.en: There are also, briefly stated, three ways affliction gives rise to karma: associated arising, directly generated arising, and enhanced arising, this last meaning that further afflictions are drawn out and further karma thereby arises. There are also, briefly stated, six things not loved: enemies, illness, unpleasant objects, the sufferings of birth and the rest, bitter but effective medicine, and virtue one is unaccustomed to. The first four should be abandoned; the latter two should be cultivated.

items.title: Section: Five Ways of Enjoying Desire, Eight Faults Desire Brings

items.zh: 復次，受用諸欲略有五種。一、領納受用，二、攝喜受用，三、尋思受用，四、貪彼受用，五、攝自受用。復次，諸欲過失略有八相。一、少味多苦多過患相，二、他所逼切苦因緣相，三、雜染受用勝因緣相，四、墮諸惡趣苦因緣相，五、尋思擾亂苦因緣相，六、受用磨滅勝因緣相，七、喪身磨滅勝因緣相，八、能障善法勝因緣相。
items.en: There are also, briefly stated, five kinds of enjoying the objects of desire: receptive enjoyment, joyfully grasping enjoyment, reflective enjoyment, craving enjoyment, and self-directed enjoyment. There are also, briefly stated, eight aspects of the fault of desire: the aspect of little flavour and much suffering and many defects; the aspect of the condition for suffering pressed upon by others; the aspect of the foremost condition for defiled enjoyment; the aspect of the condition for the suffering of falling into evil realms; the aspect of the condition for suffering from disturbance by deliberation; the aspect of the foremost condition for the loss of what is enjoyed; the aspect of the foremost condition for the loss of the body itself; and the aspect of the foremost condition able to obstruct wholesome dharmas.

items.title: Section: Desire's Six Decays, Its Thicket-Name, and Fascicle Sixty-One's Own Close

items.zh: 復次，諸欲因緣略有六種變壞。一、他所逼切變壞，二、諸界互違變壞，三、所愛有情變壞，四、身變壞，五、心變壞，六、無常變壞。復次，當知諸欲由五種相似法故，得稠林名。一、由眾多相似法故；二、由雜穢相似法故；三、由養育眾生相似法故；四、由藏竄相似法故；五、由險難相似法故。我已略說有尋有伺等三地決擇，其中處處餘決擇文，更不復現。
items.en: There are also, briefly stated, six kinds of decay in the causes and conditions of desire: decay through pressure from others, decay through the mutual conflict of the elements, decay of the beloved being, decay of the body, decay of the mind, and decay through impermanence. One should also know that desire earns the name thicket through five resembling qualities: its profusion, its mixture of defilement, its nurturing of beings, its hiding and darting, and its many dangers. I have now briefly explained the decisive discernment of the grounds with investigation and reflection, without investigation yet with reflection alone, and without either; the remaining texts of decisive discernment elsewhere on these grounds will not appear again.

blocks.text: The last short sūtras of the fascicle: how calm and insight are attained, how to listen to the Dharma, and why desire is called a thicket.

Strenuous, intermittent, and spontaneous contemplation. Master Cháng Bǎi: calm without insight subdues afflictions as a stone presses grass. One who has attained meditation may still have craving, views, pride, doubt, and ignorance.

Arrogance, unwillingness, disbelief, tiredness of body and mind, distraction, and confusion. Master Cháng Bǎi: with an arrogant mind, the water of the Dharma cannot flow in. After the talk, the mind does not go on reflecting.
Master Cháng Bǎi: calm and insight, precepts, meditation, and wisdom are goods beings do not habitually train in.
Master Cháng Bǎi: desire is the chief cause of loss of what is enjoyed, loss of life, and obstruction of good.
Master Cháng Bǎi: desires decay under outside pressure, earthquake, flood, fire, quarrels, and theft. They share five traits with a dense forest; many defilements mix in them like a tangled wood.

A sūtra on kingship, the eight sufferings, and many small teachings sorted into lower, middling, and superior. The common thread: in ruling, giving, eating, or listening, the same act can be done well or badly, and the difference is in the heart.

quiz.q: By the method of contemplation, what is the superior person's case?
options: only strenuous contemplation, the greatest effort earning the greatest merit
intermittent contemplation requiring effort
having attained spontaneous contemplation
no contemplation at all
quiz.why: Strenuous, intermittent, and spontaneous contemplation mark the three. Master Cháng Bǎi links the last to the mind's equality and effortless abiding within the nine stages. Effort is thus a stage to pass through, not the measure of superiority.

quiz.q: Calm alone is lower and insight alone middling. How does Master Cháng Bǎi account for this?
options: calm is rarer and harder, and is placed first to encourage it
the first keeps no precepts
calm alone subdues afflictions like a stone on grass; in terms of wisdom, the second has a little more prajñā
the second has more merit
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the first, with calm but no insight, subdues afflictions as a stone presses grass; insight is wisdom and calm is concentration, distinct mental factors, and by wisdom the second is higher. The first list is thus not a ranking of difficulty.

quiz.q: By the absorption dwelt within, in which does the lower person dwell?
options: worldly pure absorption, anything worldly being lowest despite its purity
defiled absorption
undefiled absorption
absorption without investigation
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: this person has attained meditation yet still has defiled states of craving, views, pride, doubt, and ignorance. The second subdues these without severing the seeds. This list is separate from the earlier one on absorptions with and without investigation.

quiz.q: Does the treatise match the ten groups to the ten things one by one? What does Master Cháng Bǎi say the seekers delight in?
options: the treatise makes no such match; he does: those seeking to accomplish need help and so love friends
the treatise matches them itself, so the lecturer adds nothing
the treatise pairs them with life
the treatise pairs them with wealth
quiz.why: The treatise lists ten things in §38 and ten groups in §39 without pairing them. Master Cháng Bǎi: those who want to accomplish need friends and colleagues, so they delight in friends. The match is his own reading, not the treatise's words.

quiz.q: Which group is wholly among the six afflictive faults of one hearing the Dharma?
options: arrogance, unwillingness, greed, hatred, envy, and stinginess, all named by the text
arrogance, unwillingness, disbelief, distress of body and mind, distraction, confusion
laziness, lost mindfulness, agitation, dullness, regret, sleep
killing, stealing, misconduct, lies, wine, idle talk
quiz.why: The six are arrogance, unwillingness, disbelief, distress of body and mind, distraction, and confusion. Master Cháng Bǎi on the first: with an arrogant mind, the water of Dharma cannot enter the high mountain of pride, and one looks down on the teacher.

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain distraction after the teaching and confusion?
options: the speaker leaves at once and misspeaks, so both are the speaker's faults, not the hearer's
not reflecting or reviewing afterwards; confusion is hearing impermanence as permanence, suffering as pleasure
dozing while hearing
not knowing the language
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: after the talk, the hearer's mind does not go on reflecting on what was taught and does not review it. When the speaker says impermanent and one hears permanent, or suffering and one hears pleasure, that inversion is confusion.

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi distinguish associated from directly generated arising, and what is enhanced arising?
options: associated is earlier leading to later, direct is simultaneous, and enhanced has karma cause affliction
all three are simultaneous
all three are at different times
associated is simultaneous, direct is earlier ignorance producing later karma, and enhanced draws further afflictions that produce karma
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: associated arising is karma and affliction at one instant; direct arising is not simultaneous, the prior moment's ignorance producing later karma; enhanced arising means that after producing karma, ignorance draws other afflictions, which produce more karma.

quiz.q: Of the six unloved things, which two should nonetheless be cultivated?
options: bitter medicine and unaccustomed virtue
enemies and illness, adversity being the true training
unpleasant objects and birth's sufferings
all should be abandoned
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: calm and insight, precepts, meditation, and wisdom are goods beings do not habitually train in. The first four, such as enemies and illness, should be avoided so that one may stay well and practice. Being unloved does not make something bad.

quiz.q: Among the eight aspects of desire, how does Master Cháng Bǎi explain the "foremost condition"?
options: 勝 means excellent, showing that desire has a fine side, half of the eight being merits
desire is a condition for nirvana
desire is the main cause of certain things, such as loss of what is enjoyed, loss of the body, and obstruction of good
desire is the main cause of heaven
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the foremost condition means desire is the chief cause of a class of things, as with loss of what is enjoyed, loss of life, and obstruction of good. All eight aspects are faults, and 勝 means chief, not excellent.

quiz.q: This is rendered "the condition for suffering that leads to falling into evil realms." What is wrong with the modification?
options: none: a certain suffering makes one fall, desire only conditioning it, as the lecture says
it is the condition for the suffering of falling, not a suffering that leads to falling
it should be "heavenly realms"
"aspect" should be deleted
quiz.why: The second and fifth aspects share this pattern, the condition for a certain suffering. Master Cháng Bǎi uses that pattern for the fifth. Here too it should be the condition for the suffering of falling into evil realms, as the English of the others has it.

quiz.q: Which group is wholly among the six kinds of decay of desire?
options: state, throne, wealth, fame, governance, and practice, as listed among the gateways of decline
form, feeling, perception, formations, consciousness, self
pressure from others, conflict of elements, the beloved being, body, mind, impermanence
earth, water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: desires decay under outside pressure, as when pursuing and guarding them meets earthquake, flood, fire, wind, quarrels, and theft; decay of mind means that enjoying them brings affliction. The list is one sentence of the treatise.

quiz.q: Why are desires named a thicket, per Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: desires were met in forests in old India, so the name comes from the place, not five traits
forests bring wealth
forests are cool
they share five traits with a dense forest; enjoyment mixes in many defilements, like a dirty, tangled thicket
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: desires share five traits with a dense forest, hence their other name. On the second, many defilements mix together in enjoyment, like a dirty, tangled wood. The treatise lists profusion, mixture, nurturing, hiding, and danger.
